note: The timing-test registry for the #3678 gate (tests/timing-assertions-lint.test.js): the permitted set of timing tests. kind 'priced-harness' files are the only files in tests/ allowed to carry wall-clock budget assertions (performance.now()/Date.now() deltas or percentiles of wall-clock samples against fixed millisecond budgets) — their whole purpose is pricing a budget, so the lint exempts them by file. Every other tests/ file must price budgets in CPU time (the #3289 process.cpuUsage pattern) or not assert on time at all; pre-existing violations outside the harness are grandfathered shrink-only in tests/fixtures/timing-assertions-baseline.json. Adding a file here is a deliberate, reviewed act: state the kind and the reason the budget must be wall-clock.

permitted.reason: The load harness: its p95 and wall-clock budgets are the priced capacity budgets the file exists to check (10x ramp latency, delivery latency, wake-lease lag). Wall-clock budgets are permitted here and only here.

Reference implementation of the sanctioned #3289 pattern: the Board list budget is priced in process.cpuUsage() time over 30 samples, so runner load cannot fail it. Listed so authors find the pattern; CPU-priced assertions are never flagged by the lint.
